# Agent Memory — Phorma Agent Studio

Global repo memory for AI agents working on this codebase. **Read this at the start of every session** (after [agent.md](../agent.md)). **Append to it after completing a feature** if you learned something a future agent should know: gotchas, repeated tasks, verified practices, dead ends. Keep entries terse — dated bullets under a topic heading. Prune entries that become wrong or obsolete.

---

## Tauri / Desktop Shell

- 2026-07-03 — `"dragDropEnabled": false` on the window in `backend/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` is REQUIRED for HTML5 drag-and-drop (palette → canvas) to work in the desktop app. Tauri defaults it to `true`, which hands drops to the OS file-drop handler; `dragover`/`drop` never reach the DOM. Works in browser, silently broken in Tauri. Needs app restart to take effect.
- 2026-07-03 — Killing a spawned process on Windows: `child.kill()` only kills the `npm.cmd` wrapper, not the node child → orphan keeps the port. Use `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` (kill whole tree). Also kill any prior run before starting a new one.
- 2026-07-03 — Spawn long-running dev processes with env `CI=true` so CLIs fail fast instead of prompting interactively (the console is output-only).
- 2026-07-03 — Strip ANSI escape codes BOTH in Rust (output reader threads) and in the frontend console service, or artifacts like `[33m❯[39m` leak into the console.
- 2026-07-03 — AS's own dev server runs on port **7322** (`tauri.conf.json` beforeDevCommand/devUrl). Phorma Code uses 7321; don't collide.
- 2026-07-07 — Updater + process plugins: `tauri-plugin-updater` and `tauri-plugin-process` added to Cargo.toml, registered in `lib.rs` via `.plugin(tauri_plugin_updater::Builder::new().build())` and `.plugin(tauri_plugin_process::init())`. Capabilities need `updater:default` + `process:allow-restart`. `tauri.conf.json` needs `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts: true` + `plugins.updater` block with `pubkey` + `endpoints`. Updater signing keypair generated via `tauri signer generate` - private key at `backend/src-tauri/.tauri/updater.key` (gitignored, NEVER commit), public key in `tauri.conf.json`. CI uses `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` + `_PASSWORD` secrets.
- 2026-07-07 — `@tauri-apps/plugin-updater` JS API (CORRECTED 2026-07-14 against installed 2.10.1 d.ts): `check()` returns an update object or null. `update.download(onEvent)` and `update.downloadAndInstall(onEvent)` BOTH take an optional progress callback with `{event:'Started',data:{contentLength}}` / `{event:'Progress',data:{chunkLength}}` / `{event:'Finished'}` payloads (accumulate chunkLength yourself). The earlier note claiming "no callback + listen('tauri://update-download-progress')" was WRONG. Then `relaunch()` from `@tauri-apps/plugin-process` (on Windows `install()` exits the app itself; relaunch is for macOS/Linux).
- 2026-07-07 — `reqwest` in `backend/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` needs the `json` feature for `.json()` on Response/RequestBuilder. Without it, `.json()` method doesn't exist and cascading type errors about `[u8]` not being `Sized` appear on `bytes_stream()` iteration (misleading - the real cause is the missing feature).
- 2026-07-07 — `Cargo.toml` has `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. Do NOT use `unsafe` blocks in Rust code - use safe crates like `sysinfo` for disk-space queries instead of FFI (`GetDiskFreeSpaceExW` / `statvfs`).
- 2026-07-07 — Streaming pattern for new Rust commands: copy `llm.rs`'s emit pattern - `tauri::Emitter` global event with `{requestId, kind, data?}` payload, cancellation via `tokio::sync::watch` channel stored in a `Mutex<Option<HashMap>>`. For `bytes_stream()` iteration, use flat `match` arms (`Some(Ok(bytes))` / `Some(Err(e))` / `None`) - nested `if let` + `while let` patterns cause type inference issues with the `Bytes` type.

## Build / Dependencies

- 2026-07-03 — All npm installs in `frontend/` must use `--legacy-peer-deps`.
- 2026-07-03 — `EACCES` on `spawn node_modules/.bin/tauri` (or any `.bin` entry) means the wrapper script lost its execute bit (mode 644 instead of 755). Happens when `node_modules` is restored from a zip/tar or copied via a sync tool that strips modes. Fix: `chmod +x node_modules/.bin/tauri` (or reinstall). The native `cli.darwin-arm64.node` is `require()`-loaded and doesn't need +x; only the sh wrapper does.
- 2026-07-03 — Build verify loop: `cd frontend && npx ng build` and `cd backend/src-tauri && cargo check`. Keep both green after every phase.
- 2026-07-03 — `@angular/cdk` must stay at v20 to match Angular core.
- 2026-07-03 — `engine/` is consumed via the `@phorma/engine` tsconfig path alias (frontend/tsconfig.json → ../engine/src/index.ts). Angular compiles it as app source; no build step. Keep engine code framework-free.
- 2026-07-03 — `backend/` needs its OWN `npm install` (installs `@tauri-apps/cli` into backend/node_modules/.bin). Without it `npm run dev` fails with "The system cannot find the path specified".
- 2026-07-03 — `cloud/` must depend on the `ai` package: the `agents` SDK dynamically imports it, and wrangler bundling fails with "Could not resolve ai" otherwise. Verify cloud changes with `npm run check` (tsc + `wrangler deploy --dry-run`) — no Cloudflare account needed; `wrangler dev` gives a full local DO for E2E.
- 2026-07-03 — Wrangler/esbuild honors tsconfig `paths`, so `@phorma/engine` resolves in cloud/ the same way as in the frontend.
- 2026-07-03 — Rust `process.rs` runs ONLY allow-listed programs (npx/npm). Extend the allow-list deliberately; never accept arbitrary program names from the webview.
- 2026-07-03 — TS structural typing: interfaces WITHOUT index signatures are not assignable to `Record<string, unknown>`. Cross-package boundary types should use `object` + per-kind casts instead.
- 2026-07-03 — `tokio::select!` requires the tokio `macros` feature in Cargo.toml.
- 2026-07-12 — Circular DI (NG0200) hazard around the run/model/cloud services: `RunControllerService → ModelTransportService → PhormaCloudService → CloudService → RunControllerService`. `CloudService` legitimately injects `RunControllerService` (to `apply()` remote run events). So services on the transport path must NOT inject `CloudService`. To read the Phorma Cloud base URL, use `loadLayout('phormaCloudUrl', PHORMA_CLOUD_DEFAULT_URL)` from `layout-storage` directly (both `ModelTransportService` and `PhormaCloudService` do this) instead of `cloud.phormaCloudUrl()`.

## UI / Styling

- 2026-08-10 - FIELD DESIGN LANGUAGE (soft/Framer-style): every PrimeNG form colour now points at a `--phorma-field-*` / `--phorma-control-*` / `--phorma-segment-*` / `--phorma-overlay-*` var defined per theme block in `styles.scss`, wired up once in `core/theme-preset.ts` (`PHORMA_SEMANTIC` + `PHORMA_COMPONENTS`, merged by `definePreset` in `app.config.ts`). Recipe: translucent fill, `border-color: transparent` on dark themes / 6% hairline on light, `shadow: none`, 8px radius, and a 1px `--p-primary-color` border as the ONLY focus indicator. Adding a theme mode = one `--phorma-field-*` block, no PrimeNG token names. GOTCHAS PAID FOR: (1) these colours MUST live in `colorScheme.light`/`colorScheme.dark`, not at the `semantic` level - PrimeNG emits the semantic block BEFORE the colour-scheme blocks in the same layer, so a semantic value loses to Aura's own on source order; (2) keep the resting `border-width` at 1px (transparent) or every field reflows 2px on focus; (3) Aura has NO `hoverBackground` for the default outlined input - only `filledHoverBackground` - so the hover/focus fill lift is a small unlayered rule block in `styles.scss`; (4) inputs with a value carry `.p-filled`, so the `filled*` tokens must be set too or valued fields diverge from empty ones.
- 2026-08-10 - `--p-border-color` IS NOT A TOKEN AURA EMITS (its hairline is `--p-content-border-color`). ~40 rules used it; the ones without a fallback were invalid at computed-value time, so `border-color` fell back to `currentColor` and rendered hairlines in the TEXT colour - a large part of why the chrome read as hard-edged. Aliased once in `styles.scss` (`:root { --p-border-color: var(--phorma-overlay-border) }`) rather than editing every call site. Use a `--phorma-*` token in new code.
- 2026-08-10 - PrimeNG's surface ramp is NOT theme-mode aware: the six theme modes only override `--phorma-*`, so `content`/`overlay`/`list`/`text` stayed global zinc (dark) / slate (light) and a Nord panel hosted a `#09090b` input. `theme-preset.ts` now retints those semantic groups per theme too. When adding a theme mode, the `--phorma-overlay-bg` / `--phorma-text` / `--phorma-hover-bg` values are what make PrimeNG overlays follow it.
- 2026-08-10 - Checkbox, radiobutton, toggleswitch, togglebutton, slider, select, multiselect and datepicker all reference `{form.field.*}`, so they inherit the field recipe automatically - but two of them break if you let them: an unchecked `p-checkbox` with a transparent border and a 5% fill is invisible (selection controls need their own `--phorma-control-border`), and `p-slider`'s track/handle are `{content.border.color}`, which is now a faint hairline. Both are handled in `PHORMA_COMPONENTS`; don't "simplify" them away.
- 2026-08-10 - Bespoke (non-PrimeNG) inputs share one recipe via the `shared/_field.scss` `chrome($radius)` mixin - `@use` it, keep only sizing/typography local. A global rule in `styles.scss` CANNOT do this job: component sheets are injected after the global sheet, so at equal specificity the component wins. Each expansion costs ~330 bytes of compiled CSS, so group selectors into ONE include per sheet where `anyComponentStyle` is tight (settings-dialog sits at ~22kB and went over with two).
- 2026-08-10 - Measuring contrast on translucent fills: token values tell you nothing, because the fill composites over a glass panel over the canvas. Screenshot the element, feed the PNG back into the page as a data URL, draw to a canvas and read pixels. Doing this caught placeholders at 2.5-2.9:1 across five themes (alphas 0.34-0.50 were too low); they are now tuned per theme to land at 3.7-3.9:1. Solarized needs the highest alpha (0.75) because Base1 over a Base02 field is a narrow luminance gap.
- 2026-08-10 - `getComputedStyle` read in the same tick as `el.focus()` returns the PRE-focus value: a focus-border check reported `transparent` and looked like a bug. Drive focus with a real `page.mouse.click` (or await a tick) before reading.
- 2026-08-10 - PrimeNG emits component theme CSS LAZILY: `--p-slider-*` vars do not exist until a slider renders. To verify a component-level token override, put the component on screen first (the slider lives in Settings > Canvas > Navigation), otherwise the token reads as an empty string and looks unset.
- 2026-08-10 - Form fields must opt out of the global `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--p-primary-color) }` rule in `styles.scss`. Browsers match `:focus-visible` on a text input even when it was focused by mouse, so the ring painted a SECOND primary line 1px outside the primary focus border on every field the user clicked into.
- 2026-07-28 — EXPANDED SIDE PANELS: Prompt / Properties / Evals / Usage each expand into a full-size dialog via `PanelExpandService` (`core/panel-expand.service.ts`, one `expanded` signal so only one can be open) + the shared `app-expanded-panel-dialog` shell (`shared/expanded-panel-dialog/`). Adding another: add the id to `ExpandablePanelId`, add a `ti ti-arrows-maximize` `.phorma-panel-icon-btn` to the panel header calling `panelExpand.open(id)`, and host the dialog in `app.html` inside `@defer (on immediate)`. The shell's `height` input takes `auto` for content-driven bodies (Properties) and a fixed `min(...)` for workbench bodies (Prompt/Evals). CRITICAL: the expanded overlay sits at `z-index: 75`, deliberately BELOW real dialogs (80) — an expanded panel is a bigger panel, not a modal, so confirms/settings summoned from inside it must layer on top. At an equal z-index the confirm lost on DOM order and was visible but unclickable.
- 2026-07-28 — Escape was globally deselecting the canvas even while an overlay was open (toolbar `onKeydown`), so closing any dialog with Esc silently emptied the selection the dialog was editing — the reopened panel came back blank. Guarded by `anyOverlayOpen()`, one `document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]')` probe. Every dialog in the app carries `role="dialog"`, so new ones are covered automatically. Any future global key handler that mutates app state needs the same guard.
- 2026-07-28 — Sharing a panel body between the sidebar and its expanded dialog: extract the body into a component with a `scope = input<string>('panel')` and route EVERY `id`/`for`/`inputId` through an `id(suffix)` helper. Both instances are in the DOM at once, so static ids silently duplicate and break every `<label for>` association. Verify with `document.querySelectorAll('[id]')` — total must equal the unique count. `PropertiesForm` (57 rewritten ids) and `AgentConfig` are the reference implementations; the panel/dialog then differ only in layout via a `layout: 'stack' | 'grid'` input.
- 2026-07-28 — A direct child of a `display: flex; flex-direction: column` scroll container needs `flex-shrink: 0` or it collapses to its own header height while `overflow: auto` hides the rest. The usage dialog's run-ledger card rendered as a 26px strip with 720px of unreachable content. Symptom to check for: `getBoundingClientRect().height` far below `scrollHeight` on a card that looks empty.
- 2026-07-28 — Chart.js options objects must be a `computed()` (not a static class field) whenever any axis bound depends on loaded data — a static field is evaluated at construction when the signals are still empty, so the bound is permanently wrong. Also: a secondary-axis bar series will auto-scale to fill the plot and bury the primary line, so cap it (`max: maxValue * 4`). And never label a time series date-only when points can share a day — the Evals trend showed three identical "Jul 28" ticks; add the clock time when `new Set(days).size < days.length`.
- 2026-07-28 — `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` immediately after `link.click()` can invalidate the blob before the browser reads it (empty/failed download). Defer with `setTimeout(..., 0)`. To E2E-verify a download without relying on Playwright download events, stub `URL.createObjectURL` to capture the blob and `HTMLAnchorElement.prototype.click` to no-op, then `await blob.text()`.
- 2026-07-28 — When surfacing per-node data from the usage ledger, remember the ledger outlives the graph (366 days of rows vs. whatever is on the canvas now), so historic rows routinely reference deleted nodes. Resolve unknown ids to an explicit "Deleted node · <short id>" label and make those rows non-clickable — a raw `node-ms4b…` id in a table reads as a rendering bug.
- 2026-07-28 — All five side panes (Properties, Prompt, Portal, Usage, Evals) are 100% PrimeNG controls: `pInputText`+`pSize="small"` on inputs, `pTextarea`+`pSize="small"` on textareas, `pButton` on buttons, plus `p-checkbox [binary]`, `p-inputnumber`, `p-select`, `p-selectbutton`. Zero native inputs/buttons and zero `span role="button"` remain — keep new fields consistent. Gotchas: `[link]` is not a pButton input (use `[text]="true"`); scope SCSS overrides as `.phorma-x__foo.p-button` and DELETE the old border/background/cursor rules or you double up on chrome; reach internals via `::ng-deep .p-inputnumber-input` / `.p-selectbutton`.
- 2026-07-28 — Destructive icon buttons should be `severity="secondary" [outlined]/[text]` with a `--danger` modifier class that goes red only on `:hover:not(:disabled)`. `severity="danger"` on every trash icon makes a panel read as a wall of warnings.
- 2026-07-28 — Never nest a `<button>` inside a `<button>` (invalid HTML, breaks keyboard nav). The Evals suite/run/result rows put the row button and its delete/action button as SIBLINGS in a `__row` flex wrapper, with the action revealed on `:hover` of the wrapper. Replaced the old `span role="button"` hack.
- 2026-07-28 — EVERY PrimeNG control in a panel needs an explicit size: `size="small"` on `pButton`/`p-select`/`p-inputnumber`/`p-checkbox`/`p-selectbutton`, `pSize="small"` on `pInputText`/`pTextarea`. Omitting it silently yields the default (larger) size, so a select renders 37px next to a 32px input in the same row and Back/Run in a header differ in height. Audit with a regex for tags lacking `size=`. Also do NOT override `font-size` on these controls in panel SCSS - the size token drives the height, so a hard-coded `0.8rem` desynchronizes inputs from the selects beside them.
- 2026-07-28 — PrimeNG checkbox/radio/toggleswitch render a transparent native `<input>` over the styled box, and the UA `cursor: text` on that overlay beats the wrapper's `cursor: pointer` (I-beam when hovering the box). Fixed globally in `styles.scss` via `.p-checkbox-input, .p-radiobutton-input, .p-toggleswitch-input { cursor: pointer }` plus a `:disabled` variant. Don't re-patch per component.
- 2026-07-28 — Two shared icon-button classes live in `styles.scss` - use them instead of per-panel sizing: `.phorma-panel-icon-btn` (1.5rem square, 0.4rem radius, for ALL panel header actions — Refresh / New suite / Expand / AI / Preview etc., paired with `severity="secondary" [text] size="small"` and NO `[rounded]`) and `.phorma-input-icon-btn` (1.85rem wide, height from the row's `align-items: stretch`, for copy/open buttons flush beside a small input, paired with `[outlined]`). Spinner: `.phorma-icon-spin` on the inner `<i>`. NEVER use `[rounded]="true"` on panel header buttons — it renders a circular pill that is inconsistent with the square assistant-panel pattern. The canonical reference is `.phorma-assist__icon-btn` in the assistant panel.
- 2026-07-28 — Don't use `float: right` for a trailing action inside a section heading - the following hint text wraps under the heading and collides. Make the label a flex row and give the button `margin-left: auto` (the Usage/Evals pattern).
- 2026-07-28 — `flex: 1` on a scrolling panel's grow section expands to `1 1 0%`, so the panel can squeeze it below its own content and the trailing hint overflows onto the next heading. Use `flex: 1 0 auto` (grow, never shrink) and `flex-shrink: 0` on the sibling sections.
- 2026-07-26 — Canvas overlays (ThinkingOverlay, AskUserOverlay, MCP warnings) reposition via `transformTick` bumped in `engine.onAfterDraw`, gated on overlays existing. When adding a NEW overlay type, add its presence check to the gate in `graph-canvas.ts` (`nodeThinking().size > 0 || pendingQuestions().length > 0 || hasMcpWarnings()`) or the overlay won't track pan/zoom. Overlay bodies render sanitized markdown via `marked` + `DOMPurify` + `DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml` — same pattern as assistant-chat.
- 2026-07-03 — Icons are **Tabler-only** (`ti ti-*`). `primeicons` is removed; PrimeNG components that render built-in icons (select chevrons, toast close, submenu arrows, checkboxes) need icon templates/`pt` overrides — audit when adding a new PrimeNG component.
- 2026-07-03 — Specular shimmer (`::after` gradient) was originally on the LEFT panel only. Right panel, terminal, status bar were plain glass. The single hairline divider is drawn by the resize handle, not a panel border (avoid double lines). REMOVED 2026-07-22: the left sidebar and toolbar shimmer `::after` gradients were stripped so ALL chrome panels (toolbar, both sidebars, terminal, status bar) are now plain frosted glass for consistency.
- 2026-07-03 — Angular templates do not support arrow functions in event bindings — use a component method.
- 2026-08-10 - Forcing `display: block` on a `p-select` host (to make it full-width in a form field) breaks the component's own `inline-flex` layout: the label and dropdown chevron stack vertically instead of sitting side by side, clipping the label to one character's height. Fix: use `display: flex; width: 100%` instead of `display: block; width: 100%` on the wrapper class. Hit this in the connection editor's "Auth mode" select (`connection-editor-dialog.scss`).
- 2026-07-03 — Literal `{` / `}` inside template attribute values (e.g. JSON placeholders) break Angular @-block parsing. Avoid braces in placeholders or use HTML entities.
- 2026-07-03 — `ToastService` has `success/warning/error/show` — there is NO `.info()`.
- 2026-07-03 — Console entry `timestamp` is an ISO string; `bottom-terminal.formatTime()` re-parses it with `new Date()`. Never store pre-formatted locale strings there.
- 2026-07-03 — PrimeNG context-menu submenus open on HOVER; Playwright synthetic clicks can't reach nested items. The palette supports click-to-add (`NodeDragService.requestAdd`) partly for this reason — keep it working.
- 2026-07-03 — Tried an SVG rainbow chasing-glow border on the prompt editor's focus state (dashed rect + hue-rotate). User rejected it on sight ("looks like shit") and it was reverted same-session. Lesson: flashy animated borders on a plain multi-line text input read as gimmicky, not premium — keep focus indication to a simple border-color change (see `.phorma-prompt__editor:focus`). Don't re-propose SVG glow effects for form inputs without being asked.
- 2026-07-04 — `ConfirmDialogService` supports a `prompt()` mode with a single text input (added for workflow naming). Pass a `ConfirmDialogInput` (initialValue, placeholder, required, maxLength); resolves to the trimmed string on confirm or `null` on cancel. The dialog component auto-focuses the input and Enter submits when non-empty. Reuse this for any rename/name flow instead of building a bespoke dialog. GOTCHA: `close()` clears `activeState` to `null` BEFORE calling `resolve`, so the `.then()` callback must NOT read `this.activeState()` — the resolution object carries `inputValue` through the resolver closure instead. Reading the signal in `.then()` silently returns `''` (the original bug that made saves always store "Untitled Workflow").
- 2026-07-06 — PrimeNG v20 button CSS variables are severity-prefixed: `--p-button-primary-background`, `--p-button-primary-hover-background`, `--p-button-secondary-background`, etc. There is NO generic `--p-button-background` or `--p-button-hover-background`. To make a `::before` overlay track the button's background across all severities/states, use `background-color: inherit` (picks up the computed `background-color` which PrimeNG swaps per hover/active/severity). `color-mix(in oklch, inherit, white N%)` does NOT work — `inherit` is not resolved inside `color-mix`. Use `background-color: inherit` + `background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,N%), transparent)` instead.
- 2026-07-23 — PrimeNG v20 `pButton` (non-outlined, i.e. primary/solid) renders an opaque `::before` overlay at `position:absolute; z-index:0; inset:0` with the button's `background-color`. In-flow children (bare text nodes AND static `<i>` icons, both `z-index:auto`) paint BELOW this overlay, so the label text AND icon are invisible on solid buttons. Fix: wrap the label in `<span class="...label" style="position:relative;z-index:1">` and give the `<i>` icon `position:relative; z-index:1` too. Outlined/secondary buttons don't hit this (their `::before` background is transparent). This is a general PrimeNG v20 gotcha, not specific to the version-history dialog — any solid `pButton` with inline content (icon + bare text, no `.p-button-label` span) will have invisible content.
- 2026-07-28 — There is now a SHARED fix for the solid-`pButton` invisible-content gotcha: add `class="phorma-btn-content"` (styles.scss) to any solid `pButton` and wrap bare label text in a `<span>`. The class sets `isolation: isolate`, pushes `::before` to `z-index:-1` and lifts `> *` to `z-index:1`. Use it instead of hand-rolling per-button `position:relative; z-index:1` rules. Detect the bug WITHOUT eyeballing: screenshot the button element, draw it to a canvas and count pixels with all channels > 200 — a solid button whose label is buried reports **0** bright pixels. Audit regex for offenders: `<button[^>]*pButton[^>]*>` filtered to matches lacking `[text]`, `[outlined]` or `phorma-btn-content` (note `severity="secondary"` on its own is still SOLID and affected).
- 2026-07-24 — Same invisible-text gotcha applies to the hand-rolled `.phorma-btn-shimmer` utility class (styles.scss): its `::before` overlay sits at `z-index:0` and the `> * { z-index:1 }` lifter only catches ELEMENT children. Bare text nodes are NOT elements, so `> *` skips them and they paint under the overlay (icon visible, label invisible). Fix: wrap any bare label text in a `<span>` inside `.phorma-btn-shimmer` buttons. Icon-only shimmer buttons (chat send, cmdk submit) are fine without a span.
- 2026-07-06 — `updatePrimaryPalette()` called in `ThemeService` constructor does NOT take effect on first paint — PrimeNG's theme engine hasn't emitted CSS yet when the service is first injected. To seed the saved palette on first paint, read localStorage synchronously in `app.config.ts` and pass the ramp to `definePreset(Aura, { semantic: { primary: ramp } })`. The `ThemeService` constructor still calls `updatePrimaryPalette` for runtime swaps, but the preset seeding prevents the flash.
- 2026-07-06 — Theme palettes are: Iris (purple, default), Azure (blue), Emerald (green), Monochrome (neutral). Retired ids: 'indigo' → 'azure', 'blue' → 'azure', 'slate' → 'iris'. Migrations live in both `app.config.ts` (`readInitialPaletteRamp`) and `theme.service.ts` (`readInitialPalette`) — keep them in sync. The Iris 500 is `#8578f6` (oklch(0.645 0.20 286), a vibrant version of #8878F2).
- 2026-07-22 — Root font-size is **14px** (`html`/`body` in styles.scss), NOT 16px. Any rem-based type floor must be computed against 14: `0.857rem`≈12px, `0.928rem`≈13px. A prior pass wrongly used `0.75rem`/`0.8125rem` (16px-root assumptions) which rendered 10.5/11.4px. Verify font floors by measuring `getComputedStyle(...).fontSize` in the live browser, never by rem arithmetic alone.
- 2026-07-22 — Panel-width persistence bug (fixed): `Sidebar.panelWidth` was `signal(270)` and `ngAfterContentInit` pushed it into the registry, clobbering the saved `leftWidth`/`rightWidth` on every startup. Hydration must read the registry per-side AFTER the `side` input is bound. The `side` input is NOT bound in the constructor (input signal reads its default 'left' there) — hydrate in `ngOnInit`, which runs before `ngAfterContentInit`'s write-back. Default width is now 320 (`DEFAULT_PANEL_WIDTH` in panel-registry.service.ts); MIN 220 / MAX 640.
- 2026-07-22 — Dark shell is "obsidian/violet", not blue-charcoal: `:root.app-dark` neutral surfaces use hue ~275 at very low chroma (canvas `#0c0a10`, card `#130f18`, node `#17131d`, glass `rgba(19,15,25,0.88)`). Keep `--phorma-accent-blue` selection accents and the azure palette option — only neutral surfaces were tinted. Matches phorma-labs.com.
- 2026-07-22 — PrimeNG `p-button` in this app: never use the `icon`/`iconPos` props (they render removed `pi pi-*` PrimeIcons). Put the Tabler icon as content: `<button pButton severity="secondary" [outlined]="true"><i class="ti ti-plus"></i> Label</button>`. Icon-only destructive → `severity="danger" [text]="true" [rounded]="true"`. Keep hero/accent buttons (green Run, OAuth Connect, runs Approve) hand-rolled to preserve their custom accent/shimmer.
- 2026-07-24 — Sidebar list row truncation pattern (skills panel = canonical): action buttons live in a `.phorma-__row-actions` container that collapses to `width:0; opacity:0; overflow:hidden` when not hovered and expands to `width:auto; opacity:1` on row `:hover`. This is the ONLY way to let the title/meta column get the full row width (so text truncates at the right edge) while still revealing actions on hover without overlap. The workflows panel previously used `opacity:0` alone on each button - they still occupied layout space (~66px for 3 × 1.6rem buttons), forcing the name to truncate far back. Fixed to match the skills pattern: wrap buttons in a collapsing `.phorma-__row-actions` span, shrink buttons to 1.4rem with 0.1rem gap, use `<span role="button" tabindex="0">` (NOT nested `<button>` - invalid HTML inside a button) with `(click)` + `(keydown.enter)` + `event.stopPropagation()` in the handler. Same pattern should be reused for any future sidebar list row with hover-revealed actions.

## Product Rules

- 2026-07-03 — Prompts are **markdown**. Render previews sanitized (`marked` + DOMPurify) — never raw `innerHTML`.
- 2026-07-03 — No Monaco, no code editors. This is not a coding tool.
- 2026-07-03 — Domain/engine code must not hard-depend on Tauri — the app must work in a plain browser (`TauriService.isDesktop` guards).
- 2026-07-03 — API keys: desktop keys live in the OS keychain via `llm.rs` (webview only sees a boolean); engine requests carry the `{{API_KEY}}` placeholder that Rust (desktop) or FetchModelClient (web) substitutes. Never log or persist raw keys elsewhere.
- 2026-07-03 — RunEvents are the single visualization contract: local engine AND (later) cloud WebSocket both feed `RunControllerService.apply()`. New run UI must consume RunEvents, not bespoke state.
- 2026-07-03 — Tool calling is native: agents get tool schemas from their tool-link edges via the engine's `ToolHost` (studio: `ToolHostService`; cloud: `CloudToolHost`). Tool loop max 8 rounds, results capped at 8KB.
- 2026-07-03 — MCP stdio transport is NEWLINE-DELIMITED JSON-RPC (not LSP Content-Length framing). Sessions live in Rust (`mcp.rs`), keyed by tool node id. Remote MCP uses the engine's `HttpMcpClient` (streamable HTTP; responses may be SSE or JSON — parse both).
- 2026-07-03 — Ollama's OpenAI-compat endpoint sends `finish_reason` without a `[DONE]` line — stream parsers must flush tool calls on BOTH signals.
- 2026-07-03 — Engine E2E testing: a throwaway `npx -y tsx script.mts` importing `./engine/src/index.js` against local Ollama is the fastest full-loop verification (no UI needed).
- 2026-07-03 — Web Search tool uses DuckDuckGo's free instant-answer API — topical coverage only. Swap in a keyed provider (Brave/Tavily) for production-grade search without touching the engine.
- 2026-07-03 — Web Search was returning "No results found" for ANY query because Wikipedia's API rejects requests with no `User-Agent` header (HTTP 403 "Please set a user-agent"). `reqwest` (Rust desktop path) and Cloudflare Workers `fetch` send NO default UA. The engine's `safeParse` silently swallowed the 403 body into `{}` → 0 results. Fix: `performWebSearch` now passes `User-Agent: PhormaAgentStudio/0.1 (https://phorma.dev)` via the `TextFetcher` signature (now `(url, headers?) => ...`). Also added `origin=*` to Wikipedia URLs for browser-path CORS. Lesson: any outbound HTTP from the engine should set a UA — many APIs (Wikipedia, GitHub, etc.) reject UA-less requests, and the failure is silent because `safeParse` masks non-JSON bodies.

## Settings System

- 2026-07-07 - `SettingControl` supports a `button` type (`{ type: 'button', label, icon? }`): the dialog renders a small outlined `p-button` on the row's control side, clicking calls `setting.set(undefined)`. Use for action-style settings (e.g. "Run setup wizard") - a toggle is NEVER the medium for one-shot actions.
- 2026-07-07 - Setup wizard (`workspace/onboarding/`) is strictly modal: no close button, backdrop click and Escape are no-ops (Escape is swallowed while visible so it doesn't leak to other dialogs/canvas). Exits are finish or explicit "Skip setup" - BOTH call `OnboardingService.finish()` which sets `firstRunDone` so the wizard never auto-opens again. The API-keys path also finishes before deep-linking to Settings. There is no plain `close()` on the service by design.
- 2026-07-04 - Application settings are registry-driven: `core/settings-registry.ts` (`SettingsRegistryService`) declares pages/sections/`SettingDef` descriptors whose get/set delegate to service signals (SettingsService, ThemeService, CanvasStateService). The Settings dialog renders generically from it - adding/removing a setting is one descriptor entry, no template changes. Bespoke UIs (API keys, palette swatches, integration creds, default model) use `customTemplate` ids mapped to @switch cases in `settings-dialog.html`.
- 2026-07-04 - Settings dialog is a bespoke two-pane overlay (`.phorma-settings`, mirrors confirm/cloud dialog pattern) - the app now has ZERO `p-dialog` usage. Controls are PrimeNG (p-toggleswitch, p-select, p-slider) with `appendTo="body"`. Opened via App menu > Settings or Ctrl+, (`SettingsDialogService.open(pageId?)` supports deep-links, e.g. `open('integrations')` from the properties panel).
- 2026-07-04 - Agent default model is TRUE INHERITANCE: `AgentNodeData.provider/model` are optional (both `workflow.model.ts` AND `engine/src/types.ts` - keep twins in sync). Engine `RunOptions.defaultModel`/`maxToolRounds` carry app settings into local runs; `CloudService.materializeDefaults()` bakes them into the spec at push time (no cloud/ changes). New agents from `node-catalog.ts` carry NO provider/model. Canvas subtitle shows "Default" when inheriting.
- 2026-07-04 - MCP preset secrets have two keychain scopes: node `mcp:{nodeId}:{envKey}` (override) and preset `mcp:preset:{presetId}:{envKey}` (app default, set in Settings > Integrations). Both pass llm.rs's `mcp:` prefix validation unchanged. Rust `mcp_connect` takes optional `preset_id` and resolves node scope first, then preset scope. Properties panel shows a status pill + collapsible Advanced group for overrides.
- 2026-07-04 - GOTCHA: an Angular `effect()` that calls a method which synchronously READS and WRITES the same signal (e.g. `refreshMcpSecretFlags` reading+setting `mcpSecretsConfigured` in browser mode) loops forever and CRASHES the page (renderer OOM). Wrap such calls in `untracked(() => ...)`. Hit twice in this feature (settings dialog + properties panel effects).
- 2026-07-04 - `anyComponentStyle` budget is 8kB compiled CSS. Comments don't count; `var(--x, fallback)` fallbacks and duplicated rule blocks do. Consolidate shared BEM variants with selector lists before fighting the budget.
- 2026-07-04 - `engine/` has no local TypeScript install: `npx tsc` there tries to fetch the bogus `tsc` npm package (interactive prompt). Use `../frontend/node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` instead.
- 2026-07-04 - macOS shortcut display: the toolbar's `onKeyDown` already accepts both Ctrl and Meta (`const ctrl = e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey`), so Cmd+key works at runtime. For display, `Toolbar.shortcut(hint)` converts `Ctrl+X` to `⌘+X` on macOS via `navigator.platform` detection; the `#item` ng-template renders `<i class="ti ti-command"></i>` + the suffix for macOS Ctrl shortcuts. Non-Ctrl shortcuts (Alt+G, Esc) pass through unchanged. The brand-mark menu (Phorma logo) is the first `p-menubar` root item with `brand: true`; the `#item` template renders the logo image for brand items.

- 2026-07-05 - Cloud provider choice is `SettingsService.cloudProvider` signal (`'phorma' | 'cloudflare' | null`, persisted as `phorma.layout.cloudProvider`). NULL means "not chosen" and drives the toolbar redirect: `Toolbar.openCloud()` sends unconfigured users to `settingsDialog.open('cloud')` instead of the Cloud dialog. Settings page id is `cloud`, custom template `cloud-provider` (two large cards when unset, tab strip + per-provider panel after).
- 2026-07-05 - `CloudDialog` branches on `settings.cloudProvider()` (fallback `'cloudflare'`): phorma branch hides ALL wrangler/worker/token vocabulary (layman copy: "Publish workflow" / "Watch live"); cloudflare branch keeps the 3-step technical flow. `CloudService.effectiveWorkerUrl` picks `phormaCloudUrl` (default `https://phorma-agent-studio-cloud.phormalabs.workers.dev`, configurable) vs user's `workerUrl`.
- 2026-07-05 - Cloud worker has two modes via `PHORMA_MODE=hosted` env: hosted = Clerk-only auth (fail closed, PHORMA_TOKEN fallback DISABLED), per-instance `ownerId` stamped on first `/workflow` push and enforced on every request/WS connect (403/4001 on mismatch). BYO mode (unset) = today's open/PHORMA_TOKEN behavior, fully backward compatible. `verifyToken` returns `AuthContext { userId }` (Clerk JWT `sub`), NOT a boolean — tenancy hangs off it. Optional `CLERK_JWT_KEY` (PEM) enables offline verification (no JWKS fetch on DO cold start); `CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES` guards azp.
- 2026-07-05 - Usage/cost pipeline: `ModelChunk` has a `usage` variant (`ModelUsage { inputTokens, outputTokens, costUsd }`); `openAiBody` requests `stream_options.include_usage` for openai/openrouter ONLY (Gemini/Ollama compat shims unverified) + OpenRouter `usage: { include: true }` (returns actual USD in `usage.cost` — authoritative billing figure, in-band). Anthropic: input_tokens at `message_start`, CUMULATIVE output_tokens at `message_delta` (take last, don't sum). Engine emits one `node-usage` RunEvent per model round; consumers sum. `RunControllerService.runUsage` accumulates for the Runs panel chip; `WorkflowAgent` sums per-run and persists `lastRunUsage` + `monthUsage` rollup in DO state (D1 ledger is the future authoritative store).
- 2026-07-05 - `cloud/package.json` declares `@phorma/engine` as `file:../engine` (was previously undeclared, resolved only via tsconfig paths — wrangler bundling needs the real dep). Verify cloud bundle with `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir=/tmp/...`.
- 2026-07-05 - PRODUCT: BYO Cloudflare stays FREE (no license gate); Phorma Cloud is the subscription product. Hosted inference should use per-tenant OpenRouter provisioned keys with credit limits (Management API), NEVER one shared runtime key. Full plan archived in session memory 2026-07-05.
- 2026-07-05 - Hosted control plane lives in `cloud/src`: `auth.ts` (shared verifyBearer/verifyRequest — DO + gateway + API all use it), `tenants.ts` (TenantStore over D1 `DB` + KV `TENANTS` cache, TIERS table, AES-GCM key encryption via `KEY_ENC_SECRET`, OpenRouter provisioning API calls), `api.ts` (`GET /api/me` Clerk-authed; `POST /api/provision|/api/deactivate` gated by `PHORMA_ADMIN_TOKEN`). The DO re-verifies ownership (defense in depth). WS auth token comes from `?token=` because the studio can't set WS headers.
- 2026-07-05 - `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` is async now: hosted mode gates on tenant status (402), monthly run count (429), cost budget (402), and requires a provisioned runtime key. `mapGraphToOpenRouter()` rewrites agent provider/model to OpenRouter slugs (`anthropic/`→, `google/` for gemini; ollama → hard error). BYO stays permissive.

- 2026-08-07 - `validateAgainstCapabilities` (engine/src/capabilities.ts) never actually read `HostCapabilities.features` before this date - `stdioMcp: false` on `CLOUDFLARE_CAPABILITIES` was pure metadata, so a workflow with a local (stdio) MCP node passed push/deploy validation and only failed at RUN time (`CloudToolHost.listTools` throws "needs a remote MCP URL"), for every trigger source (manual, scheduled cron, webhook, portal) equally - it's not a manual-trigger-only issue, the node itself is unrunnable on that host. Added a validation rule so this is now a push-time Problems console error like every other capability mismatch. Deliberately leaves run history, usage ledger and connection metadata untouched. `CloudService.deployedStatus`/`refreshStatus()`/`removeWorkflow()` back the Cloud dialog's per-workflow deploy indicator + remove button (both providers, keyed on `activeDoc()?.workflowId` like `PortalPanel` already does - null when the doc was never saved to the library, since `exportActiveSpec()` mints a throwaway id in that case). No cross-workflow "list of published workflows" was built - the DO-per-workflow-id model already lets any caller derive per-workflow status from the local library without a new registry.
- 2026-08-07 - GOTCHA: adding a new HTTP method to a route in `workflow-agent.ts` is NOT enough - the browser's CORS preflight (OPTIONS) is answered by `corsHeaders()` in `index.ts` (`Access-Control-Allow-Methods`) BEFORE the request ever reaches the DO's `routeAgentRequest`. Shipping `DELETE /workflow` without adding `DELETE` there broke it with a browser-only CORS error (curl/tests never trip preflight, so `npm run check` and Miniflare tests missed it until a regression test was added dispatching a real `OPTIONS` request). `cloud/src/workflow-agent.ts`'s own `json()` helper has its own separate CORS header set (already had DELETE) - the two lists can drift; check BOTH when adding a method anywhere under `/agents/workflow-agent/`. Regression test: `deploy-validation.test.mjs` "OPTIONS preflight CORS headers".
- 2026-08-07 - Overlay z-index bug: `.phorma-confirm` (ConfirmDialogService's dialog) was `z-index: 80`, TIED with every real dialog (`.phorma-cloud`, settings, connection-editor, etc., also 80). A confirm summoned from inside a real dialog (e.g. Cloud dialog's "Remove from cloud") lost the tie to DOM order and rendered behind it. Fixed by bumping `.phorma-confirm` to `85` (steering doc `conventions.md` updated: 75 expanded panels / 80 real dialogs / 85 confirm / 90 command palette). Any new "always on top of any dialog" surface needs its own tier here, not a reused value.
- 2026-08-07 - CREDENTIALS THAT REACH A DEPLOYED WORKER - the honest matrix, verified by reading every path. A deployed run can ONLY resolve a credential that exists as a worker secret: `CONN_<ID>_<KEY>` (connections) or `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` (remote MCP bearer, now a declared `MCP_${string}` index signature on `Env` instead of a `as keyof Env` cast). Consequences: (a) stdio MCP is impossible by design; (b) interactive-OAuth MCP is impossible in the cloud in BOTH modes - tokens live in the studio keychain via `mcp-oauth.service.ts` `mcp-oauth:{nodeId}` and `CloudToolHost.mcpFor` only ever reads `authKey`, never `authMode`. **UPDATED 2026-08-10: point (c) no longer holds for `CONN_*` - see the SecretVault entry below. It still holds for `MCP_*`, so a remote MCP node with an `authKey` in hosted mode still runs UNAUTHENTICATED and fails silently at the MCP server.**
- 2026-08-10 - CONNECTION SECRETS ON A DEPLOYED RUN, second ingestion path (`SecretVault`, spec `.kiro/specs/deployed-credential-vault/`). The reported bug: save a bearer secret in the connection editor, push to the cloud, get "Connection X is missing 1 of 1 secret values on Cloudflare Worker" and an aborted push. Correct behaviour, unactionable UX - the local value is in the OS keychain (`conn:{id}:{key}`) and the worker counts `CONN_*` env vars, and nothing in the app could set one. Now: `POST /api/connection-secrets {connectionId, secretKey, value}` encrypts with `KEY_ENC_SECRET` and stores in a `SecretVault` DO scoped `secrets:{userId}` (hosted) / `secrets:default` (BYO); `WorkerConnectionStore` reads env FIRST, vault second. Gotchas that bit or nearly bit: (a) the vault must be per OWNER not per workflow, or the operator re-enters the same key once per workflow; (b) `pushWorkflow` reads the inventory BEFORE `POST /workflow` stamps `ownerId`, so `connectionHost` needs an `ownerFallback` from `auth.userId` or a hosted tenant's FIRST deploy of a workflow reads the wrong vault and reports everything missing; (c) a new DO class needs migration `v3` in `wrangler.jsonc` top level AND `env.hosted` AND `DeployConfigService.DO_MIGRATIONS`/`DO_BINDINGS` - the generated `wrangler.byo.jsonc` REPLACES the committed config, so missing it silently drops the binding from every BYO deploy; (d) the route sits ABOVE the `store.enabled` gate in `api.ts` because BYO has no D1; (e) it refuses on a BYO worker with neither `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` nor `PHORMA_TOKEN` - an open worker treats every caller as owner, fine for `/trigger`, not for a credential store. `deploy-config.test.mjs` now derives the expected DO class list from `src/index.ts`'s export statement, so this class of drift fails a test instead of a deploy.
- 2026-08-10 - The connection editor asked for the same secret name TWICE - once as `auth.secretKey` (a pointer) and once as a declared field in the Secrets list - with nothing linking them, so a typo resolved to nothing at run time with no visible cause. Fixed by `authSecretKeyNames(auth)` (engine) + `withAuthSecretKeys` (editor): saving a connection auto-declares every name the selected auth mode points at. ADD-ONLY on purpose - removing a name the operator stopped pointing at would orphan a stored value. Do not "clean up" `secretKeys` to match auth.
- 2026-08-10 - `ConnectionSummary.missingSecretKeys` (both stores populate it) + `HostCapabilities.connectionSecretScheme` (`os-keychain` | `cloudflare-worker-env` | `none`) are what make a missing-secret finding end in an action naming the exact entry. The scheme is DECLARED data, not an inferred host id, so a new host inherits no remedy text by accident. Keep the finding's `(secret keys: ...)` fragment: `capabilities-findings.spec.ts` asserts on it.
- 2026-08-07 - `smtp` is a DECLARED BUT UNIMPLEMENTED `ConnectionType`. It is in `ALL_CONNECTION_TYPES` and therefore in every host's `connectionTypes` (so push validation lets it through), and the connection editor offers it, but nothing anywhere speaks SMTP: no `lettre` in Cargo.toml, zero `smtp` matches in `cloud/src/` or `backend/src-tauri/src/`, and `engine.ts` says outright it "keeps an SMTP client out of the engine". The `notify` node's `email` channel is an HTTPS POST to a provider API (`notifyUrl`/`baseUrl`), rejecting any non-http(s) URL. Email from the cloud = transactional API (Resend/SendGrid/Postmark) over an `http` connection, never SMTP.
- 2026-08-07 - Deploy-target findings: `CapabilityFindingsService` validated ONLY against the local host, so an undeployable node (stdio MCP being the canonical case) looked perfectly fine on the canvas and first failed at push, after the workflow was fully built. Now `localFindings` (unchanged severity, still gates local runs via `RunControllerService`) + `deployFindings` (validated against `CLOUDFLARE_CAPABILITIES`, forced to `warning`, tagged `deployOnly: true`, deduped against local messages by message text, suppressed when `cloudProvider() === null`) and `findings` = both. `deployOnly` MUST stay a warning - these fire while the author is iterating locally and must never block a local run. The canvas popover renders a "DEPLOY" tag for them.
- 2026-08-07 - PALETTE BUG (pre-existing, found by E2E): searching any MCP server name ("jira", "resend") returned "No nodes match your search". MCP presets render INSIDE the Tools group's `<section>`, but `sections()` dropped any group with `entries.length === 0` - and a preset-name query matches no CATALOG entry, so Tools vanished and took every preset with it. The Tools group must survive when `mcpPresets()` is non-empty. Regression test: `agents-palette.spec.ts`. Lesson: whenever a group's template renders extra content beyond `entries`, its empty-check has to account for that content.
- 2026-08-07 - MCP transport is now shown as an ICON, never spelled into labels (`node-catalog.spec.ts` pins that no preset label contains "(local"/"(remote"). Shared helpers in `node-catalog.ts`: `mcpTransportKind(transport)` (absent/`stdio` -> `local`, `sse` -> `remote` - matching `defaultData()`, and getting this backwards would mark every generic MCP node deployable), `MCP_LOCAL_ICON` (`ti ti-device-desktop`), `MCP_TRANSPORT_LABEL`, and `MCP_TRANSPORT_CANVAS_ICON`. Remote uses the `app-phorma-cloud-icon` SVG in the DOM, but Canvas2D paints from the icon FONT and cannot use an SVG component - hence the separate `MCP_TRANSPORT_CANVAS_ICON` map (`ti ti-cloud`). Rendered in: palette sub-group headings + per-tile pip, properties "MCP server" label, Settings Integrations card title, and the canvas kind badge (`transportGlyph`/`transportFont` on `RendererNode`, painted inside the same pill left of the `mcp-tool` text, with `bw` widened by `transportW` or the text overflows the pill).
- 2026-08-07 - Settings -> Integrations filtered on `envSchema.length > 0`, which silently EXCLUDED every OAuth preset (an OAuth credential is an interactive session, so `envSchema` is empty). The canvas warning's "Configure in Settings - Integrations" deep-link (`#integration-{presetId}`) then landed on a page with no trace of the server it was complaining about - the reported "I don't see it in the list". Filter is now `envSchema.length > 0 || authMode === 'oauth'`, and OAuth cards carry a note pointing at the node's Connect button. `node-catalog.spec.ts` pins that every OAuth preset and every `remoteAlternativeId` target is listed. Any new preset-warning source needs a matching Integrations entry or its deep-link is a dead end.
- 2026-08-07 - `pTooltip` silently does NOTHING if the component's `imports` lacks `TooltipModule` (PrimeNG directives are per-component in standalone Angular). `PropertiesForm` does not import it, so the transport pill there uses a native `title` instead; `SettingsDialog` does import it, so `pTooltip` is fine in that template. Check the component's `imports` before reaching for a PrimeNG directive in its template.
- 2026-08-07 - `angular.json` `anyComponentStyle` warning is 22kB / error 26kB (raised from 20/24 for the settings dialog's Integrations group expanders). The committed `settings-dialog.scss` was ALREADY ~20.2kB compiled before that change - it lives permanently at the warning line. Convention (from this and the prior 12kB->18kB bump): consolidate duplicated selectors FIRST, then bump the budget only for the residual, leaving headroom to the error cap. Do NOT treat this as licence to grow every component - it is scoped to a legitimately dense settings surface.
- 2026-08-07 - Integrations now groups servers into collapsible `<details>` expanders (`Remote MCP servers` / `Local MCP servers`, remote first, count pill, chevron rotates via `details[open] > .caret`). The Local/Remote tag FLOATS RIGHT of the card's head flex row (it is the third child of `__integration-head`, after icon + text), not inline in the `<h5>` - inline made it wrap under long descriptions. Deep-linked cards auto-expand their collapsed group: the anchor-scroll effect does `target.closest('details').open = true` BEFORE `scrollIntoView`, because a card inside a closed expander is display:none and unscrollable. Integration cards dropped their own border/padding (the group `<details>` is the bordered container now); stacked cards separate with a top border on the `+` sibling.
- 2026-08-07 - `.phorma-settings__hint` is indented to the field-label column (`$settings-row-indent`), so it is WRONG for a card-level note - it renders visually detached under the description. Added `.phorma-settings__integration-note` (no indent) for notes that belong to the integration card rather than a credential row.
- 2026-08-07 - `McpPreset.remoteAlternativeId` links a stdio preset to its remote twin so a deploy warning can name the fix ("Swap it for X"). Enrichment happens in `CapabilityFindingsService.withRemedy`, NOT the engine - `MCP_PRESETS` is studio data and the engine must stay catalog-free. Added `atlassian-remote` (`https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2`, OAuth, supports dynamic client registration so no `oauthSetup` needed) and `email-remote` (Resend `https://mcp.resend.com/mcp`, deliberately BEARER not OAuth because bearer is the only thing a deployed worker can resolve). Renamed the stdio ones to "Jira (local)"/"Email (local)". `node-catalog.spec.ts` pins that every `remoteAlternativeId` resolves to an existing `sse` preset with a URL.
- 2026-08-07 - LOST-UPDATE BUG (root cause of "MCP email credentials don't stick"): `refreshMcpSecretFlagsScoped` did `const next = {...this.mcpSecretsConfigured()}` -> `await` N `has_secret` IPC calls -> `.set(next)`. `GraphCanvas.mcpCredentialRefresher` fires node-scope AND preset-scope refreshes for every MCP node in one unawaited block, so several always overlap and the last to resolve discarded the others' flags. The keychain value was fine the whole time; only the flag map lost it, and re-saving (one uncontended refresh) appeared to fix it until next launch. Fix: build a local delta and `.update(current => ({...current, ...resolved}))`. Extracted `hasMcpSecret(scope, envKey)` so `settings.service.spec.ts` can stub it with per-key delays - WITHOUT staggered delays the bug is invisible, because browser mode resolves synchronously and every refresh lands in one microtask. Any signal holding a shared map that async writers touch needs `update`, never `set`.

## MCP Presets

- 2026-07-07 — Adding an MCP preset = ONE entry in `MCP_PRESETS` (`frontend/src/app/core/node-catalog.ts`). The palette, properties panel, settings-dialog Integrations, node instantiation, and the Rust stdio spawn path all pick it up automatically. No backend/model changes for stdio npx/uvx presets (Rust `resolve_command` already handles npx + uvx).
- 2026-07-07 — Presets needing a non-secret positional ARG (e.g. filesystem allowed dir) use `argFields?: McpArgField[]`. They're appended as trailing positional args after the static `args` in `mcpPresetToCatalogEntry` and rendered as labeled inputs in the properties panel via the `mcpArgFields` computed (field + absolute index into `data.args`). Don't confuse with `envSchema` (secrets, keychain).
- 2026-07-07 — Settings › Integrations only lists presets with `envSchema.length > 0` (filtered in settings-dialog.ts `mcpPresets`). No-secret presets (filesystem/git/fetch/memory/sequential-thinking) would otherwise render empty cards.
- 2026-07-07 — The `sse`/remote "Server URL" input ALREADY EXISTS in properties-panel.html (the `@else` branch of `transport === 'stdio'`). Don't rebuild it when adding remote-transport presets. Preset credential fields (bearer token) render in that same `@else` when `mcpPreset()` is truthy.
- 2026-07-07 — Remote (`sse`) MCP presets: set `transport:'sse'`, `url`, and `authKey` (the envSchema field name whose secret becomes `Authorization: Bearer <token>`). `command`/`args` stay required by the `McpPreset` type — set them to `''`/`[]`. `mcpPresetToCatalogEntry` branches sse vs stdio for defaultData.
- 2026-07-07 — REMOTE MCP BEARER AUTH crosses the trust boundary differently than stdio. stdio secrets stay in Rust (injected as env vars). A remote bearer token must reach the HTTP request in the webview, so `HttpMcpClient(endpoint, authHeaders)` takes headers and the CALLER resolves the token (keeps engine framework-free). Desktop: narrow Rust command `mcp::get_mcp_bearer(server_id, auth_key, preset_id)` returns ONLY that one secret (node-scoped then preset-scoped). Browser: `SettingsService.resolveMcpBearer` reads localStorage. Cloud: `CloudToolHost({resolveBearer})` maps authKey -> worker secret `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` (e.g. `GITHUB_TOKEN` -> `MCP_GITHUB_TOKEN`).
- 2026-07-07 — `ToolHostService.httpMcpFor` is ASYNC (resolves the bearer before constructing the client). Both call sites (`listMcpTools`, `callMcpTool`) must `await (await this.httpMcpFor(...))`.
- 2026-07-07 — Shipped remote bearer preset: GitHub (`https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`, authKey `GITHUB_TOKEN` = PAT). REMOVED Pipedream + Composio: they don't fit a static bearer (Pipedream needs a client-credentials token exchange + per-request `x-pd-*` headers at `remote.mcp.pipedream.net/v3`, one app per connection; Composio generates per-session `mcp.url`+headers via its SDK, no static endpoint). Both are OAuth/session-shaped — Phase 3+ territory, not a one-field preset.
- 2026-07-07 — INTERACTIVE MCP OAUTH (Phase 3) is split by trust boundary: pure logic in `engine/src/mcp-oauth.ts` (`McpOAuthClient`: RFC9728/RFC8414 discovery, RFC7591 DCR, PKCE S256, RFC8707 resource param, code exchange, refresh — injected `OAuthCrypto`+fetch, no DOM). Host wiring in `frontend/src/app/core/mcp-oauth.service.ts` (`McpOAuthService`). Desktop consent = Rust loopback in `backend/src-tauri/src/oauth.rs` (`oauth_loopback_start`/`_wait`/`_cancel`, `std::net::TcpListener` on `127.0.0.1:0`). Browser consent = popup + `postMessage` from static `frontend/public/oauth/callback.html` (redirect `origin/oauth/callback.html`). Loopback chosen over custom scheme (spec allows localhost + pairs with DCR).
- 2026-07-07 — `McpToolData.authMode: 'bearer'|'oauth'` selects the auth path in `ToolHostService.httpMcpFor`: `oauth` -> `McpOAuthService.validAccessToken` (auto-refresh, 60s skew); else `authKey` -> `resolveMcpBearer`. OAuth sessions stored under secret key `mcp-oauth:{nodeId}` (keychain desktop / localStorage browser), NEVER in workflow JSON.
- 2026-07-07 — Web Crypto `subtle.digest` under TS strict rejects `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` as BufferSource — copy into a fresh `ArrayBuffer` first (see `browserCrypto()` in mcp-oauth.service.ts).
- 2026-07-07 — OAuth presets: "GitHub (OAuth)" (`github-oauth`, authMode oauth, has `oauthSetup`) alongside "GitHub (token)" (PAT), plus generic "Remote MCP (OAuth)" (`remote-mcp-oauth`, empty url, DCR path). Deployed cloud runs still use the Phase 2 `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` worker-secret bearer path (interactive OAuth token reuse in cloud not yet wired). `McpPreset.command`/`args` are OPTIONAL now (sse presets omit them).
- 2026-07-07 — MCP OAuth on desktop MUST route HTTP through Rust `http_request` (webview blocks cross-origin fetch to auth servers → "HTTP unreachable"). `McpOAuthService` passes a `routedFetch` into `McpOAuthClient` (arrow fn, so the engine's `.bind(globalThis)` is a harmless no-op). `http_request` now also returns response `headers` (lower-cased) so the 401 `WWW-Authenticate` discovery hint survives.
- 2026-07-07 — RFC 9728/8414 well-known discovery inserts `.well-known/<type>` BETWEEN host and path: for `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp` it's `…/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` (path-aware), with root + OIDC `openid-configuration` fallbacks. Root-only 404s.
- 2026-07-07 — GitHub's OAuth AS does NOT support dynamic client registration, and GitHub OAuth apps require a FIXED callback URL. So: (a) desktop loopback prefers a STABLE port (7328) via `oauth_loopback_start(preferredPort)` with ephemeral fallback, and (b) `McpOAuthService.resolveClient` resolution order is user-stored client (`mcp-oauth-client:{nodeId}`) → preset `oauthSetup.defaultClient` → DCR. `fetch`+Web Crypto binding gotcha: bind default fetch to globalThis; copy Uint8Array into fresh ArrayBuffer for `subtle.digest`.
- 2026-07-07 — GitHub OAuth VERIFIED specifics (probed live): PRM at `…/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` advertises `scopes_supported` (repo, read:org, …) on the RESOURCE metadata, NOT the AS metadata — `McpOAuthService.connect` must pass `prm.scopes_supported` into the authorization request or the token has no grants. GitHub's token endpoint REQUIRES the client secret even for public clients (PKCE still binds the code — same model as GitHub's own MCP binary which bakes a public secret into the build), and returns HTTP 200 with an `error` JSON body on failure — `McpOAuthClient.tokenRequest` checks for in-body `error`/missing `access_token`.
- 2026-07-07 — OAuth preset UX: presets whose provider lacks DCR declare `oauthSetup` on `McpPreset` (`registerUrlTemplate` with `{callback}` placeholder, `needsClientSecret`, `note`, optional `defaultClient` for true one-click). The properties panel renders a numbered one-time-setup flow (open pre-filled register page → paste client id+secret) and gates Connect until a client resolves. GitHub's register URL pre-fills name/url/callback via `oauth_application[…]` query params.
- 2026-07-07 — Preset UX rules: preset-fixed `sse` URLs render as a read-only locked row (editing the GitHub endpooint only breaks it); the transport dropdown is hidden for ALL preset nodes (only generic "MCP Server" chooses); stdio preset nodes with an empty `envSchema` skip the credentials status pill (Filesystem/Git/etc. showed a bogus "Credentials missing" warning before). `ToolHostService` now throws actionable errors when an OAuth node is unconnected or a bearer preset has no token (previously silently sent no auth header → cryptic 401), and filters empty-string positional args before `mcp_connect`.
- 2026-07-07 — Email preset is `@n24q02m/better-email-mcp` (npx), single `EMAIL_CREDENTIALS` secret in `email:app-password` form (host auto-discovered). Replaced the old `email-reader` uvx server that used a confusing 4-field encrypted-password scheme.
- 2026-07-07 — Shipped stdio presets + verified sources: Filesystem/Memory/Sequential Thinking = `@modelcontextprotocol/server-*` (npx); Git/Fetch = `mcp-server-git`/`mcp-server-fetch` (uvx); Brave = `@brave/brave-search-mcp-server` (npx, v2 defaults stdio, `BRAVE_API_KEY`); Postgres = `postgres-mcp` (uvx, crystaldba, `--access-mode=restricted` for read-only, secret `DATABASE_URI`); Slack = `@zencoderai/slack-mcp-server` (npx, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` + non-secret `SLACK_TEAM_ID`). Slack `users.list` (and any paginated API whose cursor lives at the JSON tail) lost its `next_cursor` under the slice, so the model couldn't continue paging. Made it a named `DEFAULT_TOOL_RESULT_CAP_CHARS` (8000) + per-agent `AgentNodeData.toolResultCapChars` override (clamped to `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CAP_CHARS` = 200000). - 2026-08-07 — Jira preset = `uvx mcp-atlassian` (sooperset/mcp-atlassian, MIT, 5.7k stars, 200 contributors, releases within weeks). Env: non-secret `JIRA_URL` + `JIRA_USERNAME`, secret `JIRA_API_TOKEN`. Leaving the `CONFLUENCE_*` vars out of `envSchema` is deliberate — the server auto-scopes its tool surface to whichever product is configured, so Jira-only config yields Jira-only tools. - 2026-08-07 — ROOT CAUSE of "OAuth MCP node connects fine, still 401s once deployed": `CloudToolHost.mcpFor` (`cloud/src/workflow-agent.ts`) only ever reads `data.authKey` (static bearer -> `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` worker secret) — it never checked `data.authMode === 'oauth'`. An OAuth session (GitHub OAuth, `atlassian-remote`/"Jira & Confluence", `remote-mcp-oauth`) lives in the desktop keychain or browser localStorage and NEVER reaches the worker, so a deployed call goes out with NO `Authorization` header and the MCP server 401s. This was invisible at push time because `validateAgainstCapabilities` (engine/src/capabilities.ts) had a rule for stdio MCP (`stdioMcp` feature) but none for OAuth MCP. FIXED: added a 6th `HostCapabilities.features` flag `mcpOAuth` (true desktop+browser — `ToolHostService.httpMcpFor` already resolves `McpOAuthService.validAccessToken` on both — false on `CLOUDFLARE_CAPABILITIES`), a matching validation rule (mirrors the stdio one, same file), and a `CloudToolHost.listTools` throw naming the real constraint instead of the bare "HTTP 401". Adding a 6th feature flag means every `HostCapabilities` object literal needs it (only 3 exist, all in `capabilities.ts`) and `capabilities.spec.ts`'s hardcoded `FEATURE_FLAGS` array needs the new key too, or `'%s declares...all N feature flags'` fails.
- 2026-08-07 — The `atlassian-remote` ("Jira & Confluence") preset description literally claimed "Runs in the cloud, so scheduled and deployed workflows can use it" and the local `jira` preset's description told users to "use the remote ... server for scheduled workflows" — BOTH FALSE per the finding above (OAuth session never reaches the worker). Fixed both description strings. Also fixed `CapabilityFindingsService.withRemedy` (frontend/src/app/core/capability-findings.service.ts): it suggested swapping a `remoteAlternativeId` in as "the fix" without checking whether that alternative is itself OAuth (Jira's only remote alternative is) — recommending it just traded one deploy finding for the identical one on the swapped-in node. Now skips the remedy sentence when `alternative.authMode === 'oauth'`.
- 2026-08-07 — SEPARATE real bug found while investigating the above, likely why the user saw "still shows as a warning in the canvas" right after a successful Connect: `GraphCanvas.mcpCredentialRefresher` (frontend/src/app/workspace/canvas/graph-canvas.ts) only re-reads OAuth connection state when `this.graph()` changes. Connecting/disconnecting OAuth from the properties panel (`PropertiesForm.connectOAuth/disconnectOAuth`) touches no node data, so the canvas's cached `oauthConnected` map went stale until an unrelated graph edit forced a recompute. Fixed by adding `McpOAuthService.connectionChangeTick` (a signal bumped on successful connect/disconnect) and having the canvas effect track it alongside the graph. If you add another component that caches "is node X OAuth-connected" locally, track this tick too instead of polling once on selection.
- 2026-08-07 — FOLLOW-UP same day: "Remote" now means "cloud-deployable" everywhere, not just "over the network". `McpTransportKind` (node-catalog.ts) is `'local' | 'remote' | 'oauth'`; `mcpTransportKind(transport, authMode?)` takes a 2nd param and an sse+oauth preset is its own `'oauth'` kind with its own icon (`MCP_OAUTH_ICON` = `ti ti-key`, deliberately NOT the cloud glyph). Every consumer needed the split: canvas badge (`graph-to-scene.ts`), properties-panel transport pill, `agents-palette` sub-groups (now Remote / Sign-in (OAuth) / Local), Settings › Integrations groups (same 3-way, `settings-dialog.ts/.html`). Renamed `atlassian-remote` to "Jira & Confluence (OAuth)" (matches "GitHub (OAuth)"/"GitHub (token)"). Audited every `transport:'sse'` preset: `github-oauth` and `remote-mcp-oauth` were ALSO mis-bucketed as deployable "Remote" before this — only `github` (token) and `email-remote` (Resend, bearer) are genuinely deployable. `CapabilityFindingsService.withRemedy` no longer suggests a `remoteAlternativeId` swap when the alternative's `authMode === 'oauth'` (it doesn't fix deployability, it just moves the identical finding).
- 2026-08-07 — `http-tool` (engine/src/tools.ts) gained real generalization to actually make cloud-deployed API tools viable: (1) `params?: HttpToolParam[]` (name/description/required) — declaring params replaces the single `input` fallback with one named string property per entry, spliced into its own `{{name}}` token in BOTH url and body independently (needed because Jira's add-worklog endpoint needs an issue key in the url path AND a JSON body at once — one shared `{{input}}` token can't hold two different values). No `params` = old single-`{{input}}` behavior, byte-identical, so every existing node keeps working. (2) `connectionId?: string` — the HOST (studio `ToolHostService`, cloud `CloudToolHost`) resolves it and calls the SAME `applyConnectionAuth` that `http-request`/`notify` already use, so an agent-callable HTTP tool can finally carry real Basic/Bearer auth instead of a secret hardcoded into `node.data.headers` (an actual OWASP-relevant fix, not just a feature). Added `'http-tool'` to `CONNECTION_KINDS` in properties-form.ts — the EXISTING shared connection-picker section just works, no new picker UI needed. (3) new export `withConnectionBaseUrl(url, conn)` — a plain `{{baseUrl}}` string-replace convention (not template syntax) so a tool's url can read `{{baseUrl}}/rest/api/3/search` and the real site address lives once on the Connection, not copy-pasted into every node. `engine/src/tools.spec.ts` is a NEW file (tools.ts had zero test coverage before this).
- 2026-08-07 — GOTCHA: engine files are type-checked under the FRONTEND's stricter tsconfig (`noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature`) because the frontend build compiles `engine/src` directly — `engine`'s own `tsc`/vitest run does NOT catch this. A `Record<string, unknown>` cast means every property access, including WRITES (`properties.input = {...}`, not just reads), needs bracket notation (`properties['input']`) or `ng build` fails with TS4111 while `cd engine && npx vitest run` stays green. Always run frontend's `ng build` after touching `engine/src`, don't trust engine's own checks alone.
- 2026-08-07 — Shipped a second `WORKFLOW_TEMPLATES` entry, `tpl-jira-safety-net` ("Jira Time-Log Safety Net"), as the concrete proof this all works: 2 schedule triggers (cron has no timezone — Oct-Mar fires 08:00 UTC = 19:00 AEDT, Apr-Sep fires 09:00 UTC = 19:00 AEST, both hand off to the same agent so only one fires per evening), 1 agent, 4 `http-tool` nodes against Jira REST v3 (search / get-worklogs / add-worklog, `connectionId` deliberately left blank for the user to fill in), plus the `email-remote` (Resend, bearer) MCP preset for the report. A schedule-triggered run's `input` is ALWAYS `''` (`WorkflowAgent.scheduledRun()` calls `this.trigger('', undefined, 'schedule')`) and NO prompt anywhere gets a real date injected, so there's a 5th unauthenticated `http-tool` hitting `timeapi.io` (verified live before committing to it — `worldtimeapi.org`, the other well-known option, failed to even fetch) as the agent's mandatory first call for ground-truth "today". `workflow-templates.spec.ts` (NEW file, first test coverage for `workflow-templates.ts`) asserts the built spec clears `validateAgainstCapabilities` against `CLOUDFLARE_CAPABILITIES` with ZERO findings — an actual regression test for "genuinely deployable", not just a comment claiming it.
- 2026-08-07 — Test-writing gotcha (caught by the new spec, on the PRE-EXISTING IAS template too, not just the new one): the `node()` template helper stores raw port ids (`${nodeId}-${portKey}`, no suffix) but `connect()` stores connector ids WITH the `-in`/`-out` suffix appended. Comparing them as raw strings fails; use `portBaseId()` (exported from `@phorma/engine`) on the connector side first.

## Phorma Cloud Model Provider (Local-Run Inference Proxy)

- 2026-07-12 — `phorma-cloud` is a new `ModelProviderId` (added to BOTH `engine/src/types.ts` AND `frontend/src/app/core/workflow.model.ts` — keep the structural twins in sync). It routes local-run inference through the Phorma Cloud `/api/infer` proxy, billed against the tenant's subscription credits (OpenRouter runtime key). No BYO key needed. Curated models only (stored as full OpenRouter slugs): `openai/gpt-5.5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`, `google/gemini-3.5-flash`.
- 2026-07-12 — `ModelTransportService.create()` returns a `CompositeModelClient` that intercepts `request.provider === 'phorma-cloud'` → `PhormaCloudModelClient` (POSTs the engine-built OpenRouter-shaped wire request to `${phormaCloudUrl}/api/infer` with the Clerk session JWT as Bearer; streams SSE back; parses with `createStreamParser({ ...request, provider: 'openrouter' })`). All other providers delegate to the existing Tauri/Fetch BYO path. The engine calls `stream()` per-node with `request.provider`, so the composite branches at runtime — no engine changes needed for the routing decision.
- 2026-07-12 — Cloud proxy `POST /api/infer` in `cloud/src/api.ts`: verifies Clerk JWT (`verifyRequest`), gates on subscription+quota via shared `resolveHostedInference()` (in `tenants.ts`), injects the tenant runtime key, forwards to OpenRouter, tees the response stream (one copy to the client, one parsed for the `usage` block), meters via `recordRun`. The tenant key NEVER leaves the worker. Security: authenticate every call + enforce quota exactly like `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` (402/429) — otherwise it exposes unauthenticated inference on the tenant's key.
- 2026-07-12 — CRITICAL GOTCHA (fixed): `/api/infer` metering (`meterInferenceStream`) reads the SECOND tee'd stream copy to extract usage AFTER the client's copy finishes. It MUST run via `ctx.waitUntil(...)`, NOT a bare `void promise.catch()`. Without waitUntil, Cloudflare tears the worker down as soon as the client finishes reading its copy → the metering promise is killed before `recordRun` writes to D1 → usage silently stays at 0 (symptom: Runs panel shows "N credits" for a run but Settings quota bar stays "0 / 1000"). Required threading `ExecutionContext` through `fetch(request, env, ctx)` → `handleApiRequest(..., ctx)` → `routeApiRequest(..., ctx)`. NEEDS WORKER REDEPLOY to take effect (`wrangler deploy --env hosted`).
- 2026-07-12 — Post-run quota refresh: `RunControllerService.finishRun()` calls `phormaCloud.refresh()` (after a 1.5s delay to let the waitUntil D1 write land) ONLY when `runUsage().phormaCloud` is true. Before this, the quota bar/account chip only refreshed on dialog-open/sign-in, so a just-completed Phorma Cloud run's spend never showed until you reopened Settings. `RunControllerService` injects `PhormaCloudService` directly — safe (no circular DI: PhormaCloudService only injects ClerkService, reads phormaCloudUrl from localStorage not CloudService).
- 2026-07-12 — CRITICAL GOTCHA (fixed): `recordRun` had a hardcoded `runs_used + 1` bump, called from BOTH `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` (correct: 1 per deployed workflow run) AND `meterInferenceStream` (the `/api/infer` local-run proxy — WRONG). Every local Phorma Cloud inference call (per agent node × per tool-call round) was inflating the monthly run count, so a few local debug runs pushed users to e.g. 7/300. Fix: `recordRun` takes `countsAsRun?: boolean` (default true); the SQL now uses `VALUES(?,?,?,?)` + `runs_used + excluded.runs_used` with a bound `runIncrement` (0 when countsAsRun=false, 1 otherwise). `/api/infer` passes `countsAsRun: false` — local runs consume CREDITS (cost) only, never the run allowance. `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` is unchanged (defaults to true). NEEDS WORKER REDEPLOY. Existing inflated `runs_used` rows in D1 don't self-correct — reset manually if needed (`UPDATE quotas SET runs_used = 0 WHERE tenant_id=? AND month=?`).
- 2026-07-12 — `OPENROUTER_SLUG_PREFIX`, `toOpenRouterModel()`, and `resolveHostedInference()` were lifted from `workflow-agent.ts` into `tenants.ts` as shared exports (the DO + the `/api/infer` proxy both use them). `mapGraphToOpenRouter` in `workflow-agent.ts` handles `phorma-cloud` nodes (prefix `''`, provider→openrouter) so deployed workflows with phorma-cloud nodes work in hosted mode. BYO own-Cloudflare deploy: phorma-cloud errors clearly (no tenant key).
- 2026-07-12 — `openAiBody` in `engine/src/model.ts` checks `request.provider === 'openrouter'` for usage accounting (`stream_options.include_usage` + `usage: { include: true }`). Added `phorma-cloud` to those checks so the proxy gets usage/cost data for metering. The `phorma-cloud` adapter in `ADAPTERS` reuses `openAiCompatible('https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions', false)` — `requiresKey: false` because the local client never holds a key (the proxy does).
- 2026-07-12 — `PhormaCloudService.sessionToken()` is the public method to resolve a fresh Clerk JWT for the proxy (added 2026-07-12). Don't access `clerk.session$` from outside the service — it's private. The method returns `null` when signed out.
- 2026-07-12 — BYO live model fetch: `ModelTransportService.listModels(provider)` mirrors `listBedrockModels` — desktop → Rust `list_provider_models` cmd; browser → direct fetch (CORS best-effort, falls back to free text). Rust `list_provider_models` in `llm.rs` supports anthropic/openai/gemini/openrouter. Gemini uses `?key=` query param; Anthropic uses `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version` header; OpenAI/OpenRouter use Bearer. Registered in `lib.rs` `generate_handler!`.
- 2026-07-12 — UI gating: Phorma Cloud provider only appears in the picker when `phormaCloud.subscribed()` is true. In both `prompt-panel.ts` and `settings-dialog.ts`, `providers` changed from a plain array to a `computed()` signal that filters `MODEL_PROVIDERS`. GOTCHA: templates MUST call it as `providers()` not `providers` — `ng build` catches this (TS2322: `Signal<...[]>>` not assignable to `any[]`). Phorma Cloud is excluded from `keyedProviders` in settings (no API key needed).

## Usage Credits (abstraction over real USD inference cost)

- 2026-07-12 — Phorma Cloud NEVER shows dollars to the user. `TierLimits` now has `monthlyCredits` (round marketing number, the ONLY billing unit displayed) alongside `monthlyCostUsd` (real spend cap → OpenRouter key limit, analytics-only). Tiers in `cloud/src/tenants.ts` TIERS (plus tier REMOVED 2026-07-19): starter {1000cr,$4}, pro {3000cr,$12.60}, team {10000cr,$44}. Base burn = 125 credits/$1 at the ORIGINAL (pre-margin-fix) ratio; higher tiers include a volume bonus (pro +5%, team +10%) baked into a LARGER USD budget so a credit buys more real inference — credit numbers stay round regardless of the USD side. Prices (margin ref, not yet enforced): $20/$60/$200 → 80%/79%/78% margin.
- 2026-07-12 — MARGIN FIX: initial pass used `monthlyCostUsd` ≈ 40% of price (60/58/56% margin). Dropped the ratio to ~20% of price to hit a 75-80% target — this ONLY changes `monthlyCostUsd` per tier (halved: 8→4, 16.32→8.16, 25.2→12.6, 88→44). `monthlyCredits` and every display/API/frontend surface is UNTOUCHED — that's the entire point of the credits abstraction: the real budget can move without any user-visible change.

Frontend `PhormaCloudProfile.quota` mirrors both; `PhormaCloudService.creditsFraction` (renamed from `costFraction`) + `creditsPerUsd` computed (derives burn rate from quota, falls back to 125). Cloud DO consumer of node-usage (`workflow-agent.ts`) only reads `event.usage`, so the new field flows through the relay untouched.
